headline: Sequence language models for RNA, DNA, and molecules are adding structured objectives
label: Genomic Language Models
summary: Recent preprints apply joint-embedding objectives, state-space fusion, and pretrained encoders to RNA, DNA, and molecular sequence prediction tasks.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the reuse of pretrained sequence language models, with changes made either to the training objective or to how representations are combined and fed into downstream prediction. JEPA-DNA adds a joint-embedding predictive latent objective to genomic foundation model training and reports gains in linear probing and zero-shot evaluation. CrossLLM-Mamba instead fuses ESM-2 and RiNALMo embeddings through bidirectional Mamba state-space encoders for RNA-protein, RNA-small molecule, and RNA-RNA interaction prediction. The antisense oligonucleotide benchmark examines input choice directly, comparing SMILES and DNA sequence representations across general-purpose and chemistry LLMs. DRfold2 pairs a pre-trained RNA language model with a denoising module for single-sequence structure prediction. MolDeBERTa's chemistry-informed SMILES pretraining is a separate molecular case. What is new is the explicit design of the objective, the fusion, or the input encoding rather than the base model alone.
